title: Circle of Live at MUTEK Mexico
excerpt: An immersive real-time visual environment for the four-hour Circle of Live session at MUTEK Mexico 2025.
description:
For the four-hour Circle of Live session at MUTEK MX 21 in October 2025, I made the real-time visuals and light environment in Hall A of Maravilla Studios, Mexico City, with multimedia artist and lighting designer Pavel Zmuchila and choreographer Alejandra Metztli.
The images ran in TouchDesigner off my own LiDAR scans of the city, captured over a day of cycling an Ecobici with cameras strapped to it, along Reforma and through Roma and Chapultepec. Four more LiDAR scanners stood around the venue during the show, so the pre-recorded city and the live room fed the same system. Pavel drove the light from a GrandMA desk blended with TouchDesigner bitmaps for the pixel fixtures, everything merged into one DMX output.
> Eight dancer platforms circled the musicians, and Metztli's Butoh choreography followed natural elements and the Fibonacci spiral. The rule we set ourselves was never to overload the senses: when the dancers led, the visuals softened; when the music rose, the light took the room.
> Working from scanned data means the city is already in the machine before the night starts. What the evening decides is which parts of it come back, and from an angle no camera could have stood in.
credits: Real-time visuals and LiDAR: Jaco Schilp / Studio Schilp. Light: Pavel Zmuchila. Choreography: Alejandra Metztli, with eight dancers. Programmed with Damián Romero. Circle of Live: Sebastian Mullaert, Pantha du Prince and Leafar Legov. Founded by Sebastian Mullaert. MUTEK MX 21 Nocturne, Hall A, Maravilla Studios, Mexico City, 10 October 2025. Photos: Diego Figueroa, Leo Luna and David Barajas.

insight.title: Planning and instinct
insight.intro: MUTEK MX spoke to the three of us about how the night in Hall A was built: Pavel Zmuchila on light, Alejandra Metztli on choreography, and me on the real-time images.

a.text: That idea immediately aligned with what MUTEK MX was looking for: something that balanced the digital with the physical.

qa.q: How did Circle of Live's improvisation shape the work?

a.text: This helped us respond intuitively to what was happening on stage. Everyone reacted live, always checking if there was room to add something or if it was better to hold back.

qa.q: What were you after with the circular design?

a.text: It was important to think about four elements: the physical sensation of the space, the lighting, the visuals, and the choreography.

qa.q: How do you prepare for operating it live?

a.text: The process was a mix of planning and instinct. The three of us had long conversations about how the night might unfold.

qa.q: What did Maravilla Studios give you?

a.text: Its scale allowed the circular design and 360-degree experience to truly feel at home.
One of the biggest challenges was making sure we didn't overwhelm people.
I worked with TouchDesigner to create real-time images using data from LiDAR scans of Mexico.
